Area.evidence_source: All participants described that surviving their suicide attempt provided them with the courage to be themselves and instilled in them an increased sense of autonomy. Being acknowledged by others after their suicide attempt facilitated this shift. For example, Brian said: People started believing in me and actually seeing who I really am, not just the emo kid starting varsity with dark hair and everything. People start seeing me as a person with feelings. That is why I stopped. I don't have (suicidal) tendencies any longer. Johan said that his recovery meant 'coming clean' about his failures and 'manning up to the fact that you did something wrong'. He describes this as an empowering experience, which strengthened his identity. For the participants who identified as gay, 'coming out' about their experience of suicide helped them to 'come out' to family members about their sexual orientation. All participants construed the suicide attempt as having helped them to become more independent from their parents and free to develop an identity separate from their parents. Brian said: 'I could be myself, I could have my own sense of identity, not be overshadowed by parents and stuff.'
